column2: On the authority of Abū ʿAbdillāh Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Anṣārī (may Allah be pleased with them both) that a man asked the Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace), saying:

“Do you think that if I pray the obligatory prayers, fast Ramaḍān, treat the lawful as lawful and the unlawful as unlawful, and do nothing more than that, I will enter Paradise?” He said: “Yes.” Reported by Muslim.
The meaning of “I treat the unlawful as unlawful” is: I avoid it.
And the meaning of “I treat the lawful as lawful” is: I do it believing it to be lawful.
“That a man”: he was al-Nuʿmān ibn Qawqal.
A-raʾayta (“do you think”): tell me.
Al-maktūbāt (“the obligatory prayers”): the five prescribed prayers.
“And fast Ramaḍān”: refrain during its days from whatever breaks the fast, with an intention.
“Treat the lawful as lawful”: do it believing it to be lawful.
“And the unlawful as unlawful”: avoid it.
“And do nothing more than that”: of voluntary deeds.
“Will I enter Paradise?”: from the outset, without punishment, since entry as such depends [only] on tawḥīd.
Naʿam (“yes”): you will enter Paradise.
The printed text reads قوفل; the name is al-Nuʿmān ibn Qawqal (قوقل), as in the other commentaries.
Whoever carries out the obligations and refrains from what is unlawful enters Paradise.
The texts to this effect are mass-transmitted.
It is permissible, in general, to leave voluntary deeds if it is not out of disregard for them, though this does not alter the fact that one who leaves them has deprived himself of great gain.

The Companions and those after them used to persevere in doing the Sunnahs and virtuous deeds as they persevered in the obligations, and did not distinguish between them in seizing the reward. The jurists needed to mention the difference only because of what follows from it: whether a repetition is required or not, and whether punishment is feared for leaving it
or not, if it is left in some way.

It has been said that the Prophet ﷺ refrained from pointing this questioner to the Sunnahs and virtuous deeds only to make things easy for him, since he was new to Islam, lest too much of that should drive him away;
and he knew that once he was established in Islam and Allah had opened his heart, he would desire what others desired. Or [it was] lest he believe that the Sunnahs and voluntary deeds are obligatory.
